tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. The only numbers in this README come from checks that need no keys, copied from [`docs/EVALUATION.md`](docs/EVALUATION.md). 84 85 ## Install the CLI 86 87 Needs **Node 22 or newer** (built on Node 24), **pnpm 11.7.0** (pinned in `package.json` → `packageManager`; for example `npm install -g pnpm@11.7.0`) and git. 88 89 ```sh 90 git clone https://github.com/parthchilwerwar/notary.git 91 cd notary 92 pnpm install 93 pnpm notary --help 94 ``` 95 96 **Quick start, no keys.** The keyless walkthrough on recorded fixtures runs the whole pipeline against an in-process simulated API with model doubles, labels everything as fixture data, and writes only to the gitignored `packages/core/runs/demo/`: 97 98 ```sh 99 pnpm notary demo --fixture 100 pnpm --filter @notary/web dev # then open http://127.0.0.1:5173/app/certificates 101 ``` 102 103 **With keys.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env` (gitignored; Dodo Payments in test mode only) and check the setup: 104 105 ```sh 106 cp .env.example .env 107 pnpm notary doctor # one neatlogs test span (needs NEATLOGS_API_KEY) 108 pnpm notary doctor --llm # model provider, the three role models, one tiny call per role 109 ``` 110 111 A keyed command with a missing variable stops with `BLOCKED: not set` (exit 3) before any network call. A docs page can say a refund amount is in units when it's in cents, that a timed-out request wasn't processed when it was, or that a list returns everything when it stops at a page cap. None of these crash anything: every call returns 200, every trace looks green, and the damage turns up later as a double refund in the payments dashboard. 116 117 ## How it works: Read → Test → Challenge → Certify → Enforce 118 119 Deterministic code makes every decision. Models only propose hypotheses and review beliefs. 120 121 1. **Read.** Every concrete promise in the Crustdata and Dodo docs becomes a machine-checkable claim, quoted and linked ([`src/contracts/`](packages/core/src/contracts/)). A recon sweep records cheap calls, and a deterministic checker compares each response with each claim: same exchanges in, same anomalies out. A field path that doesn't exist in the response counts as *not observed*, never as "honored". 122 2. **Test.** One batched reflector call proposes 2–3 rival explanations per anomaly; claims that behave as documented get code-built rivals ("honored" vs. the suspected defect). Probes are chosen by a cost-aware score, and every prediction is hashed into SQLite **before** the HTTP call. Fixed verdict rules feed a Beta(α, β) belief per claim; only confirmed, informative probes move it, each distinct probe design counts once. 123 3. **Challenge.** A different, stronger model (or a headless Claude Code session) reads only the raw probe records and tries to refute each candidate belief: uphold, narrow its scope, or downgrade it. Every cited probe must also pass an evidence check against its recorded span. 124 4. **Certify.** Each surviving belief becomes a **certificate**: the claim, the doc text and link, a verdict ("matches docs" or "contradicts docs: docs say X, observed Y"), its scope, the evidence (probe and trace ids), the adversary's verdict and a sha256 over the content. Unproven claims get a "no certificate" entry with the reason. When later evidence un-learns a belief, its certificate is **revoked** with the triggering evidence. `pnpm notary export --certificates` writes the certificates, revocations and a per-tool **Notarized API Report** ([`export/REPORT.md`](export/REPORT.md)). 125 5. **Enforce.** Certificates on the "contradicts docs" side compile into guards (transform, require_param, precheck, retry_policy, paginate_fully, block) that wrap every Dodo and Crustdata call. A money action runs only if every certificate it depends on is active; otherwise it's **held** with an evidence pack. Before a write a guard would rewrite, a re-verification sentinel re-runs the certified experiment, so an API that changes mid-run revokes the certificate and holds the action instead of moving the wrong amount. 126 127 ```mermaid 128 flowchart LR 129 R["Read
doc claims + recon + deterministic checker"] --> T["Test
rival hypotheses, commit-then-run probes, Beta beliefs"] 130 T --> C["Challenge
adversary on raw probe records + evidence check"] 131 C --> F["Certify
certificates, revocations, Notarized API Report"] 132 F --> E["Enforce
guards + belief gate + re-verification sentinel"] 133 E -- "API changed: belief un-learns" --> F 134 E --> B["Run bundle
sha256, replayable offline"] 135 ``` 136 137 The commands: `notary notarize --tool ` (Read, Test, Challenge), `notary export --certificates` (Certify), `notary run --queue …` (Enforce), `notary replay` (reproduce offline), `notary demo --fixture [--scenario change-api]` (the whole flow on a clearly labelled simulated world). 138 139 ## Results 140 141 Every row links to [`docs/EVALUATION.md`](docs/EVALUATION.md), which `pnpm notary export` generates from hash-verified run bundles. # Notary — PRD

Oct 10, 2026 · Parth

## Summary

Notary is an autonomous billing-ops agent that won't touch money until it has proven, by experiment, how its tools actually behave. It works a queue of customer requests (refunds, plan changes, credits) end to end, using Crustdata for company context and Dodo Payments (test mode) for execution.

**One-liner:** *An agent that won't touch money until it has proven how its tools actually behave.*

Before any irreversible action, Notary verifies the exact tool behaviors that action depends on, such as refund units, retry safety and pagination limits. Verified beliefs compile into guards that wrap every API call. No verified belief means no action: the request goes to a human with evidence attached.

**How these docs are organized**

- **PRD (this file):** what we build, for whom, and how we know it works.
- **TDD (`docs/TDD.md`):** architecture, data model, the notarization loop, interfaces and stack.
- **Build Plan (`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`):** phase-by-phase itinerary for the 48 hours, split between Claude Code (agent core) and Codex (dashboard UI), with ready-to-paste prompts.

The idea builds on the pattern that won Syndicate by Maximor Track 1 (Skeptic), and pushes it into what Skeptic listed as next steps: live third-party APIs, real per-call cost, cross-tool transfer and drift detection, all inside a real end-to-end task.

## Problem and users

Agents trust tool documentation by default, and when the tool moves money that trust becomes the most expensive bug in the system. A docs page can say a refund amount is in units when it's in cents, that a failed request was not processed when it was, or that a list returns everything when it silently stops at a page cap. An agent following the docs then double-refunds, refunds 100x too much, or misses an existing refund.

These failures don't crash anything. Every call returns 200, every trace looks green, and the damage shows up later in the payments dashboard.

**Who it's for**

- **Primary:** small SaaS teams and solo founders who want an agent to handle billing ops (refunds, credits, plan changes) without a human watching every action.
- **Secondary:** any team running agents against third-party APIs they don't control, where doc drift is a standing risk.

**Why now:** agents are moving from read-only tasks into irreversible actions, and the hackathon's own theme is "agents you'd trust to run without you watching." Trust has to be earned per tool behavior, not assumed from docs.

## Goals, non-goals and success metrics

Notary succeeds if run 2 makes zero unsafe money actions that run 1 made, at lower cost, with every claim backed by a trace.

**Goals**

1. Finish a real billing-ops queue end to end: enrich, decide, execute or hold, report.
2. Verify tool behaviors by pre-registered experiment before any irreversible action depends on them.
3. Get measurably better and cheaper across runs through persisted beliefs and guards.
4. Transfer defect patterns learned on one tool (Crustdata) to speed up probing the next (Dodo).
5. Make every number reproducible offline from recorded traffic.

**Non-goals (this weekend)**

- Live-mode payments. Dodo runs in test mode only.
- Supporting any API beyond Crustdata and Dodo.
- A hosted multi-tenant backend. The dashboard reads exported run bundles.
- Formal expected-information-gain math. A greedy, cost-aware probe score is enough.

**Success metrics**

| Metric | How it's measured | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsafe money actions | Duplicate refunds, wrong-unit amounts, missed existing refunds in the seeded queue | Run 1 baseline > 0; run 2 = 0 |
| Belief precision | Notarized beliefs that match a confirmed real behavior | ≥ 0.8, false beliefs = 0 |
| Unguarded call sites | Calls to a guarded operation not wrapped, found via entire-graph callers | 0 |
| Cost per queue run | Crustdata credits + Bedrock tokens per run, from neatlogs | Run 2 lower than run 1 |
| Probes to confirm on tool 2 | Probes needed on Dodo with vs. without Crustdata-learned priors | Fewer with priors |
| Automation rate | Requests executed safely without a human | Reported honestly, not maximized |
| Reproducibility | `notary replay` from a clean clone reproduces headline numbers | Exact match |

Negative or withdrawn results are kept and published, as the strongest Syndicate winners did.

## Core flows

There are four flows: the queue job, the notarization loop that gates it, offline replay, and viewing results in the dashboard.

**Flow A: Work the billing queue (the end-to-end task)**

1. Load a queue of customer requests (refund, partial refund, plan change, credit).
2. Enrich each customer's company via Crustdata and map it to a policy tier.
3. Decide the action from the policy (approve, partial, deny, escalate).
4. Check required beliefs for that action. All notarized: execute in Dodo test mode through the guards. Any missing: hold and escalate with evidence.
5. Write a run report: decisions, actions taken, holds, costs, trace links.

**Flow B: Notarize a tool behavior**

1. Recon turns doc claims into a machine-checkable contract.
2. The contract checker compares each live response to the contract and flags anomalies, with no LLM.
3. The reflector proposes two or three rival explanations per anomaly, in one batched call.
4. The probe designer picks the experiment that best separates rivals per credit spent.
5. The prediction is committed and logged before the probe runs.
6. The verdict updates the belief's confidence. Uninformative observations confirm nothing.
7. The adversary, on a stronger model, tries to refute the belief. Only survivors are notarized.
8. Notarized beliefs compile into guards and a corrected tool spec.

**Flow C: Replay offline**

1. A judge clones the repo and runs `notary replay`.
2. Recorded traffic stands in for live APIs. No keys, no credits.
3. Headline numbers reproduce exactly, and a drift fixture shows a belief being un-learned.

**Flow D: Watch it in the dashboard**

1. Open the hosted dashboard, or the local one during a live run.
2. Browse the queue, beliefs board, probe log, runs comparison and economics.
3. Click any belief or decision through to its neatlogs trace.

## Unit economics from real runs

7 real bundles (4 live, 3 replay). Live spend: $0.1263 model USD, 62 Crustdata credits, 15897 tokens. Crustdata credits have no USD price, so they are reported next to model USD, never converted.

| Figure | Value | How it is computed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cost per run | $0.0316 model USD + 15.5 Crustdata credits | Model USD (executor + reflector + adversary) and Crustdata credits summed over live real bundles, divided by the number of live bundles. Replays are excluded: they spend nothing new. |
| Cost per notarized belief | $0.0253 model USD + 12.4 Crustdata credits | Model USD and credits of every live notarize bundle, divided by the distinct notarized beliefs in each tool's newest full notarize bundle (beliefs persist across runs, so they are counted once). |

## How the plan is built in cfo.ai and comes back

cfo.ai has no REST API and no API key. Data goes in as a CSV upload (a documented data source) and comes back as a file Ari produces for download, or over its MCP server (`https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`, browser OAuth, approved account). The round trip:

1. Sign up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks (then cancel the subscription in Settings → Billing, per the hackathon rules).
2. Run `pnpm notary economics`. It writes `export/cfo-inputs.csv`: one row per real run with model USD by role, tokens, Crustdata credits, unsafe actions and held actions, straight from the bundles.
3. In cfo.ai, open Connections → Add → Integrations → Upload and choose `export/cfo-inputs.csv` (or attach it to an Ari message and pick "Data source"). Ask Ari to confirm the import finished.
4. Ask Ari to build the plan from that data source (prompt below): pricing per monitored API contract, COGS per contract, cost of incidents prevented, a monthly revenue and COGS projection, cash and runway. Review and adjust the assumptions on the Page.
5. Ask Ari for the plan as a downloadable CSV in Notary's import format (prompt below; header `section,key,label,period,value,unit,detail`). Download the file card. Optionally Share the Page (Share → Create link) and put the link in a `meta,share_url` row.
6. Run `pnpm notary economics --cfo-import <downloaded.csv>`. The plan lands in `packages/web/public/economics.json` (hash-pinned, with the file's sha256 and the import time), on the dashboard's Business page and in this file.

```text

Build a business plan for Notary, a certification layer that monitors API contracts for AI agents, on a Page named "Notary plan":
1. Three pricing tiers, priced per monitored API contract per month.
2. COGS per monitored contract per month from the live rows (model_usd plus crustdata_credits at our Crustdata credit price).
3. Cost of incidents prevented: unsafe_actions avoided times a cost per incident.
4. A 12-month projection of revenue and COGS, and cash balance with runway in months.
Ask me for any assumption you need (contracts per tier, growth, credit price, cost per incident, starting cash, monthly burn).
```

# Entire in Notary

[Entire](https://entire.io) records AI agent sessions next to the commits they produce. With Entire enabled, a commit made during a tracked Claude Code session gets an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer, and Entire saves a checkpoint for it: the transcript, the prompts, the files the agent touched and the token usage. The Entire CLI also ships an official code-graph plugin, `entire graph`.

Notary uses Entire for three things:

| Use | What happens | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Checkpointed adversary reviews | The adversary's `session` backend runs a headless Claude Code review in the repo and commits the verdict (`adversary: <verdict> <beliefId>`). Entire checkpoints that commit with the reviewer's session, so each review sits next to the belief it judged, with its full transcript. | [`packages/core/src/adversary/session.ts`](../packages/core/src/adversary/session.ts) |
| Checkpointed build sessions | Every Claude Code session that commits in this repo is checkpointed the same way. That is the build history Entire is meant to show. | `.claude/settings.json`, `.githooks/` |
| Guard coverage (FR-17) | `notary guards coverage --backend entire` asks Entire's code graph for every call into a raw Dodo or Crustdata client method. Anything outside the guard wrapper fails the check. | [`packages/core/src/guards/coverage.ts`](../packages/core/src/guards/coverage.ts) |

`pnpm notary export --entire` publishes the checkpoints and the coverage result to `packages/web/public/evidence/entire.json` ([schema](../packages/core/src/schema/entire.ts)). The Report page shows them under **Receipts → Review checkpoints**.

## What is installed

Checked on 2026-10-12, Windows 11:

| Component | Version | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entire CLI (`entire.exe`, `git-remote-entire.exe`) | 0.11.4 (go1.27.1, windows/amd64) | Official GitHub release [entireio/cli v0.11.4](https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.11.4), `entire_windows_amd64.zip`. SHA-256 `c46e4c61b55780c3d3b8192cf8bec67c436b64a4adf181a739ec38b74d4e99c7` matches the release's `checksums.txt`. Copied to `~/.local/bin` (user-local, already on PATH). |
| entire-graph plugin | v0.4.0 | `entire plugin install graph`: the official plugin index, [entireio/entire-graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph), checksum-verified by the CLI. Installed to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin`. |

No account and no login are needed for local checkpoints or `entire graph`. `entire login` is only for entire.io features (cross-repo search, dispatch, the web viewer). It has not been run.

## Setup on a new machine

```sh
# 1. Install the CLI (pick one; the docs list all of them: https://docs.entire.io/installation)
#    Windows: download entire_windows_amd64.zip from https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases,
#             check it against checksums.txt, put entire.exe and git-remote-entire.exe on PATH
#    or:      irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
#    macOS:   brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
#    Linux:   curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
entire --version                       # Entire CLI 0.11.4

# 2. The code-graph plugin
entire plugin install graph
entire graph version --json            # {"provider":"entire-graph","version":"v0.4.0"}

# 3. In the repo. The project settings are committed, so a fresh clone only needs the local hooks:
entire enable --agent claude-code --telemetry=false --checkpoint-push-remote origin
entire status                          # ● Enabled · branch main · Agents · Claude Code
```

Step 3 is what was run in this repo. It wrote:

| File | Committed? | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.entire/settings.json` | yes | `enabled`, `telemetry: false`, checkpoint store `git-refs`, and `commit_linking: "always"` (added by hand, see below). No secrets. |
| `.entire/.gitignore` | yes | Keeps `tmp/`, `settings.local.json`, `metadata/`, `logs/` and `redactors/local/` out of git. |
| `.entire/settings.local.json` | no (ignored) | `checkpoint_push_remote: origin` for this clone. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | yes | Nine Claude Code hooks (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, …) that call `entire hooks claude-code <event>`, and do nothing if `entire` is not on PATH. |
| `.githooks/prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`, `pre-push` | yes | Entire's git hooks. This repo sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, so Entire wrote them there. The existing `pre-commit` secret check is untouched. Each hook is a no-op without `entire` on PATH. |

**`commit_linking: "always"`.** Entire's default is `prompt`: when a commit follows agent work, the prepare-commit-msg hook asks `[Y/n/a]` on the terminal. The adversary's verdict commit is made by Node with no terminal, so the hook waited forever (observed live). With `always`, every commit made while Entire tracks a session is linked without asking.

**Pushing.** With `checkpoint_push_remote: origin`, the pre-push hook pushes the checkpoint refs along with `git push`. Checkpoints contain session transcripts. Entire redacts secrets before anything leaves the machine ([security](https://docs.entire.io/security)), and the GitHub repo is private. Run `entire configure --skip-push-sessions` to keep checkpoints local.

## How checkpoints map to agent sessions

```
Claude Code session (session_id = S)        hooks: .claude/settings.json → entire hooks claude-code …
   │  edits files; Entire snapshots them on a shadow branch (entire/<sha7>-<hash6>, local only)
   ▼
git commit  ──prepare-commit-msg──►  "…\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 01M4PYAG60V4ZBFR9WN79VAWB1"
   │
   └─post-commit──►  checkpoint 01M4PYAG60V4ZBFR9WN79VAWB1 → refs/entire/checkpoints/B1/01M4PYAG60V4ZBFR9WN79VAWB1
                      (session S, transcript, prompts, files touched, tokens)
```

- Checkpoint ids are 26-character ULIDs (legacy: 12 hex). `entire checkpoint list --json` lists the ones on the current branch, and `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json` returns metadata only: files touched, model, token usage.
- For Claude Code, Entire's session id is the `session_id` that `claude -p --output-format json` prints. The session backend stores that id as the bundle's `adversary.sessionId`, so a review in a run bundle, its verdict commit and its Entire checkpoint share one id.
- `reviewWithSession` reads the trailer back after committing (`git log -1 --format=%H%n%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)`) and returns `{ commit, checkpointId }` as `entire` on the outcome. `checkpointId` is null when Entire did not checkpoint the commit. The review never depends on Entire.
- `notary export --entire` publishes only **committed** checkpoints: an id carried by an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on the current branch. While a session is live, `entire checkpoint list` also returns its temporary shadow snapshots (40-hex ids) whose `message` is the latest prompt text. Those are never published, and the message shown is always the git commit subject.

### Verified end to end

On 2026-10-12, in a scratch clone of this repo with Entire enabled, `reviewBelief({ backend: "session" })` ran on the real belief `belief-crustdata.enrich.headcount-total-integer` from the real bundle `notarize-crustdata-20261012T011404Z`. Headless Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) read the inbox packet and wrote the verdict `downgrade`: the cited probes never vary the claim's `fields` parameter. The verdict commit `e6cb269` got `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4PYAG60V4ZBFR9WN79VAWB1`. `entire checkpoint explain` shows session `f5cf4a6a-…`, which is the CLI's `session_id`, with files touched `adversary/verdicts/belief-crustdata.enrich.headcount-total-integer.json`. That run found two bugs, both fixed:

1. The `--allowedTools` rules are relative to the working directory. Given an 8.3 short path (`C:\Users\PARTHC~1\…`), Claude Code denied the inbox Read and refused to invent a verdict. `reviewWithSession` now resolves the repo root with `realpath.native` first.
2. The `commit_linking: prompt` hang described above.

The clone and its checkpoint are scratch data and are not in this repo. On `main`, the first checkpoints come from the first commit made under a tracked session, or from the first `pnpm notary notarize --tool <name> --adversary session` run.

## Guard coverage with `entire graph`

```sh
pnpm notary guards coverage --backend entire     # auto picks entire when `entire graph version` works
```

The backend runs one bulk call:

```sh
entire graph edges --repo <root> --format ndjson --worktree --relation CALLS,ASYNC_CALLS,CONSTRUCTS
```

It keeps the relations whose target is a public method of `CrustdataClient` or `DodoClient` (symbol id `…:TypeScript:<file>:method:<Class>.<method>`) and whose caller is under `packages/core/src` or `packages/core/scripts`. Each one is an UNGUARDED call site. The guarded route is dynamic (`client[method]` inside `wrap`), so no static call is legitimate. For a method that does have raw callers, the exact lines come from `entire graph neighbors --symbol <Class>.<method> --direction in --format json`. A `CONSTRUCTS` relation to a client class outside `src/tools/index.ts` is a raw construction. A file Entire could not parse fails the check if it is scanned source. Other skipped files are listed and ignored: a one-line JSON adversary inbox file trips `E_MINIFIED`.

Result on this repo (2026-10-12, working tree on `0ce991d`):

```
notary guards coverage  backend: entire
  entire graph edges (entire-graph v0.4.0, working tree): 7822 call and 377 construct relations scanned, 2 reach a raw client; …
Totals: 33 sites, 26 guarded, 7 raw-by-design, 0 UNGUARDED (18 ops)
unguarded_call_sites = 0
```

The two relations that reach a raw client are `createTools()` constructing the two clients in `src/tools/index.ts`. The site list is identical to `--backend tsc`. With a deliberate raw call planted in a scratch clone (`client.createRefund(…)` and `new DodoClient(…)` in `src/entire-probe-raw.ts`), both backends report the same two UNGUARDED sites, and the entire backend gives the exact line (4) from `neighbors`. The captured output is the test fixture in `packages/core/test/fixtures/entire/`.

Cost: every `entire graph` query re-indexes a dirty working tree, about 50 s idle and up to about 5 min under load. That is why the backend makes one bulk call and not one `neighbors` call per method, which would take about 18 minutes.

## Docs vs reality

| Docs or earlier assumption | Reality (Entire CLI 0.11.4, entire-graph v0.4.0) |
| --- | --- |
| `entire graph` is part of the CLI (DECISIONS #61, #102) | It is the official plugin `graph`. Install it with `entire plugin install graph`. |
| `neighbors` has no `--format` flag (docs, #99) | `--format json\|text\|agent`. JSON is the default when piped. Text starts with `Index: cache-…`. |
| One `neighbors` call per method | Each call re-indexes the dirty tree (~50 s), so the backend uses one `entire graph edges --worktree` pass. |
| Checkpoints live on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (PRD, BUILD_PLAN "entire/* branches") | The default store is `git-refs`: one ref per checkpoint under `refs/entire/checkpoints/`. The `branch` store is legacy. `refs/heads/entire/<sha7>-<hash6>` is a live session's shadow branch, not a checkpoint. |
| `entire enable` then commit is enough | The default `commit_linking: prompt` asks on the terminal, so a commit made without a terminal hangs. Set `commit_linking: "always"`. |
| — | `entire checkpoint list --json` also returns live shadow snapshots (40-hex ids, prompt text as the message) when nothing is committed yet. |

## Showing it in the demo video (2:00–2:15)

1. Terminal: `entire status`. It shows Entire enabled for Claude Code on `main`.
2. Terminal: `git log -3 --format='%h %s%n%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)'`. The commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
3. Terminal: `entire checkpoint explain <id>` on an `adversary: …` commit. It shows the reviewer's session, its prompt and the verdict file it touched. Say: "Every review is checkpointed."
4. Terminal: `pnpm notary guards coverage --backend entire`. Show `unguarded_call_sites = 0` and the `entire graph edges` line. Say: "entire-graph proves no money call skips a guard." Pre-run it before recording, because it takes about a minute.
5. Browser: `/app/report` → **Receipts → Review checkpoints**. It shows the checkpoint rows (id, time, session, commit, files touched) and the coverage figure from `entire.json`.

Before recording, run `pnpm notary export --entire` after the last commit, so the page lists that commit's checkpoint.

# Self-audit (P9)

Oct 10, 2026. A hostile review of the repo at `12b376e` plus the fixes listed below, run before judges see it. Every claim here comes from reading the code or running a command; the commands are listed in [Commands run](#commands-run). A follow-up pass on top of `77f5ce5` worked through the remaining open findings that don't need keys. Its fixes are marked "commit pending".

**Bottom line.** No API keys were ever available, so there is **no real evidence**: no cassettes, no live bundles, no notarized beliefs, no headline numbers. This audit therefore checks the *code paths* that would produce evidence. It found 6 places where a belief or result could move without the evidence the rules require. All 6 are now fixed with tests. The follow-up pass fixed 3 more (A-10 static allow-list, A-19, A-22). What can't be defended without live runs, or needs an owner decision, stays open with the reason given.

## Evidence integrity: real bundles

| What was checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/core/fixtures/cassettes/` | Does not exist. 0 cassettes. |
| `packages/core/runs/` | Only `notary.sqlite`: anomalies 0, hypotheses 0, probes 0, run_meta 0, run_items 0. The `beliefs` table was never created. |
| `packages/web/public/bundles/` | Only `sample-42.json` (`sample: true`, `kind: "sample"`, disclosure "SAMPLE DATA — synthetic"). |
| Notarized beliefs to audit (cited probes varied the parameter, controls behaved, nothing rests on an uninformative observation) | **None exist.** Nothing to audit, so nothing was downgraded. The enforcing code was audited instead (A-01 to A-04). |

## Findings

Severity: Critical = could disqualify the submission; High = a belief, number or safety rule could be wrong; Medium = a weaker guarantee than claimed; Low = defense in depth; Info = verified, noted for reviewers.

| ID | Area | Severity | Finding | Evidence | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A-01 | Beliefs | High | Evidence that failed the FR-10 check kept its +1 on α/β. The belief reverted to `hypothesis`, but its confidence still counted the invalid probe. A later **uninformative** probe re-ran the status check and promoted it to `candidate` on that invalid weight (Beta(4,1) with 2 valid probes). | `src/beliefs/store.ts:568` (`applyEvidenceCheck`) | **Fixed** (95aed48). # Deploying Notary's agents to AWS

Status: **prepared, not yet run against AWS.** Every script stops with `BLOCKED: AWS credentials not set` (exit 3) until credentials exist. Nothing in this repo has created an AWS resource yet. The container entry point (`src/hosted-main.ts`) has been run locally against the real LiteLLM proxy, but the Docker image itself has not been built on this machine: the Docker daemon wasn't running.

## What runs where

| Agent | Model role (env) | Where it runs on AWS |
|---|---|---|
| Notary Chat | `chat` (`NOTARY_MODEL_CHAT`, falls back to `NOTARY_MODEL_REFLECTOR`) | **API service**, always on: ECS Express Mode (Fargate + HTTPS load balancer) |
| Executor (Ask Notary's model role) | `executor` | API service (`POST /api/ask`) |
| Reflector, Adversary, Executor (queue) | `reflector`, `adversary` | **Agents task**: a one-off ECS Fargate task (`notary notarize` / `notary run`) started by `deploy/aws/run-agents.sh` |
| Guard | none (a deterministic rule) | Runs inside the processes above |

The models are reached through the LiteLLM proxy, the same as on your laptop. AWS hosts the agents' code and loop, not the models. If you later set `NOTARY_LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock`, `deploy.sh` also creates a task role with `bedrock:InvokeModel`.

## Why ECS Express Mode

- **App Runner is out.** AWS closed it to new customers on 2026-04-30 and points new projects to ECS Express Mode ([availability change](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apprunner/latest/dg/apprunner-availability-change.html)).
- **Express Mode fits the API.** One `create-express-gateway-service` call gets you an ECS service on Fargate, an internet-facing ALB with TLS at `https://<service>.ecs.<region>.on.aws/`, autoscaling, CloudWatch logs and canary rollbacks. ECS secrets come from Secrets Manager. Long-lived SSE streams work through an ALB.
- **AgentCore Runtime is a poor fit for now.** Bedrock AgentCore Runtime wants a container that serves `POST /invocations` and `GET /ping` on port 8080, built for **ARM64**, with inbound auth through IAM SigV4 or JWT ([service contract](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-service-contract.html)). Notary's API is a multi-route REST + SSE server with conversation state, a read-only dashboard API and a separate batch-agent workload. Fitting it into AgentCore would mean an adapter for each agent and a JWT issuer. Express Mode runs the existing server unchanged. If AgentCore becomes a requirement, the chat loop (`src/chat/agent.ts`) is the piece to wrap behind `/invocations`.

## Security design (the hosted site is read-only)

- **No approvals.** `GET/POST /api/approvals/**` are not mounted (404). `POST /api/runs` returns 405. Chat's `list_approvals` and `get_approval` report "unavailable" on the hosted site, so even a read-only view of held actions is off.
- **Ask and chat need a bearer token.** `NOTARY_HOSTED_TOKEN` is at least 32 characters. `put-secrets.sh` generates it with `openssl rand -base64 48` and stores it in Secrets Manager as `notary/prod/NOTARY_HOSTED_TOKEN`. ECS injects it at task start. The server compares it in constant time, and it is never logged or put in a span. The localhost + session-token rule of `notary serve` is unchanged. Hosted mode is a separate entry point (`src/hosted-main.ts`), not a flag on `serve`.
- **Read endpoints stay open**, as they are locally: bundles, runs, certificates, timelines, health and `/ping`. They serve hash-verified real bundles only.
- **CORS:** exactly the origins in `NOTARY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Each must be https; plain http is accepted only for localhost.
- **Secrets never touch the image.** `.dockerignore` excludes `.env`. `put-secrets.sh` creates one Secrets Manager secret per variable, passing each value through a 0600 temp file that it deletes right after; a value is never echoed or put on a command line. `deploy.sh` reads only secret **ARNs** (`describe-secret`), never values. The execution role may read `notary/prod/*` and nothing else.
- **The API task gets only what it needs:** `LITELLM_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_BASE_URL`, `NOTARY_HOSTED_TOKEN`, and optionally `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. Crustdata and Dodo keys go only to the agents task, so chat's live lookups say "Not connected" on the hosted site.
- **Spend caps:** `NOTARY_MAX_USD` (default `0.25` in `config.env`) caps model spend per chat message and per agents run. `NOTARY_ASK_RPM` limits chat messages per minute per task. The process-wide `NOTARY_LLM_RPM` / `NOTARY_LLM_CONCURRENCY` limiter applies to every model call.
- **Dodo stays in test mode:** `NOTARY_MODE=test` and the test base URL are fixed in the agents task definition.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Dockerfile` | Two stages, `node:22.20.0-bookworm-slim`, pnpm 11.7.0 via corepack. Installs only `@notary/core` from the frozen lockfile and runs as the `node` user. Default `CMD` is the hosted API on :8080. |
| `.dockerignore` | Keeps `.env`, `node_modules`, local `runs/`, SQLite files and docs out of the build context. |
| `deploy/aws/config.env.example` | Names, sizes and model ids. No secrets. Copy it to `config.env`. |
| `deploy/aws/lib.sh` | Preflight: credentials (BLOCKED, exit 3), AWS CLI, region, `sts get-caller-identity`. |
| `deploy/aws/put-secrets.sh` | `.env` → Secrets Manager, one secret per variable. Generates `NOTARY_HOSTED_TOKEN`. |
| `deploy/aws/stage-data.sh` | Copies the real run bundles (`<id>.json`, `index.json`, `timeline.jsonl`) into `deploy/aws/data/runs`, which is gitignored and baked into the image. |
| `deploy/aws/deploy.sh` | ECR repo, image build and push, IAM roles, log group, cluster, then creates or updates the Express service. |
| `deploy/aws/run-agents.sh` | Runs `notary notarize` / `notary run` as a Fargate task. |
| `deploy/aws/render.mjs` | Renders the container and task-definition JSON. Secrets are referenced by ARN only. |
| `deploy/aws/iam/*.json` | Trust policies, the secrets read policy, and the optional Bedrock policy. |

## Steps (when credentials arrive)

Prerequisites: AWS CLI v2, Docker with buildx, Node 22+, `openssl`, and an IAM principal that may manage ECR, ECS, IAM roles, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs and EC2 describe calls.

26 docs/video/SCRIPT.md
# Notary — 3-minute explainer (faceless)

Draft 1 · narration ≈ 430 words (≈ 2:55 at a calm 150 wpm) · voice: AI narrator (ElevenLabs) · no face on camera.

Every number on screen comes from the exported runs (`packages/web/public/`), shown with the footnote
"Measured on Notary's evaluation suite" (the suite's APIs and planted quirks are documented in
`docs/EVALUATION.md#evaluation-suite`).

| # | Time | Narration (voice) | On screen |
|---|------|-------------------|-----------|
| 1 | 0:00–0:20 | AI agents are starting to move real money. They refund customers, change plans, issue credits. And they learn how to do it from API docs. But docs and reality drift apart. A refund endpoint that "returns the amount in dollars" might really take cents. A retry that "is safe" might pay twice. | Sky open, headline "No certificate, no money *moves*." → a transcript row: refund sent 100× too small; a second row: duplicate refund, both flagged red. |
| 2 | 0:20–0:40 | Notary is an agent that won't touch money until it has proven how its tools actually behave. It works in five steps: read, test, challenge, certify, enforce. | Five-step bar lights up in turn; "Notary" wordmark. |
| 3 | 0:40–1:05 | First, it reads the docs and turns every promise into a claim it can check. Then it tests. Before each call, Notary commits a prediction — written down and hashed, so it can't be changed afterwards. Then it calls the real API and compares. When the observation doesn't match, that's not a log line. It's evidence. | Real "Predict, then test" card: "Committed 08:49:28", expected *rejected* → observed *clamped*, red "Mismatch" pill. |
| 4 | 1:05–1:25 | A second model, the Reflector, proposes what might be going on. A stronger third model, the Adversary, tries to knock every explanation down. Only beliefs that survive the challenge, backed by repeated evidence, become certificates. | Reflector hypothesis card → Adversary counter-test card → "Survived 1 of 1 challenge" → seal stamps on a real certificate. |
| 5 | 1:25–1:55 | Here's the dashboard. This is a real run of the billing queue. Every step is in the transcript: the request, the tool, the decision. When an action needs a behaviour Notary hasn't certified, the Guard holds it. No certificate, no money moves. This refund was held because Notary never certified how this API pages its results. | UI walkthrough: Run page, transcript scrolls, cursor opens refund q03 held card ("no certificate for dodo.payments.page-size-max-100"). |
| 6 | 1:55–2:15 | Each certificate shows exactly what it covers, and the experiments behind it. If the API changes later, Notary re-checks, and the certificate is revoked — before the next payment goes out. | Certificates page → certificate detail (scope, probes, adversary review) → revocation card from the change-api world. |
| 7 | 2:15–2:35 | Held actions go to a person. The approval desk shows why each one was held and the evidence behind it. A human approves or rejects, and that decision is recorded too. | Approvals page: held card, cursor hovers Approve (typed-amount confirm shown). |
| 8 | 2:35–2:50 | And you can just ask. Notary Chat reads the runs, the certificates and the approved docs, and answers with citations to the exact records. It can explain anything. It can't move money. | Chat: question typed, three lookup steps tick, cited answer streams; citation chip highlights its step. |
| 9 | 2:50–3:00 | On our evaluation suite, the agent without Notary made nine unsafe money moves. With Notary: zero, and nine refunds safely held for review. Notary. Let your agent prove it first. | Stats 9 → 0, 9 held (footnote); dither chart; closing sky, wordmark, github.com/parthchilwerwar/notary. |

## Production notes

- Voice: calm, confident, neutral; ElevenLabs text-to-speech with word timestamps (captions and cursor moves sync to words).
- UI walkthrough: the real dashboard driven by Playwright in replay, cut into the Remotion timeline with zooms and the animated cursor.
- Music + SFX: synthesized in code (as in the showreel), ducked under the voice.
- Captions burned in + `notary-explainer.srt`. Output `docs/media/notary-explainer.mp4` (1080p).

# Notary hackathon-readiness audit (read-only, done 2026-10-12 around 09:30 IST) ## Verdict **Not ready to submit as it stands. The engineering is strong, but the submission isn't.** The real notarize loop has run live on Crustdata and Dodo, it is traced to neatlogs, and its coverage check runs on the real Entire CLI. That is genuinely good and unusually honest work. But a strict judge today finds these problems: - the repo is private; - there is no ~2.5-minute video; - cfo.ai is not done; - there is no real queue run, so the core "naive unsafe → guarded 0" story exists only on fixtures; - the README says "no live run recorded"; - `pnpm notary replay` from a fresh clone **exits 1 and prints "TAMPERED OR INVALID BUNDLE"** seven times; - `pnpm test` fails in a fresh clone. My estimate is about 40–45/100 today. It could reach about 65–75 if the must-do list below lands. ## 1. Scorecard (PRD weights) | Criterion | Score | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **The agent (30%)** | 5/10 | **Real:** 4 live bundles plus 3 replays in `packages/web/public/bundles/`.
• `notarize-crustdata-20261012T011404Z`: 11 claims, 3 deterministic anomalies, 4 probes, 1 notarized belief.
• `notarize-dodo-20261012T012315Z`: 15 probes, 4 notarized.
• Adversary (claude-opus-4.6) **narrowed** all 5 beliefs and upheld none.
• 5 real certificates, all "matches docs", 0 "contradicts docs" (`certificates/report.json`: certified 5, unproven 21).
• Committed predictions sit on the probe spans (`runs/*/spans.jsonl`, `notary.prediction` + `predictionHash`).
**Missing:** FR-1. There is no real `run --queue` bundle, naive or guarded; recovery and escalation are shown on fixtures only. | | **neatlogs (part of 25%)** | 6/10 | **Real:**
• 30 notarize spans exported (7 for crustdata trace `9db41ecd…`, 23 for dodo), all `exported:true`.
• 56 chat spans (AGENT/TOOL/CHAIN/WORKFLOW).
• The doctor smoke span.
• DECISIONS #204 says trace `b7944cd2b6279b78ab010355aea8cf67` was read back with 56 spans. That trace id is **not in any repo data or local `runs/`**, so I couldn't verify it.
**Gaps:**
• Bundle `traceLinks` are `{}`. There is no neatlogs UI URL or screenshot anywhere. The spans files are in gitignored `runs/`, so a judge sees nothing.
• `evidence.json` notes are stale (they still mention wrapBedrock and "not read back").
• The run1-vs-run2 comparison is impossible without queue runs. | | **Entire (part of 25%)** | 5/10 | **Real:**
• CLI 0.11.4 plus graph plugin v0.4.0; `guards coverage --backend entire` gives 33 sites and 0 unguarded.
• 2 checkpoints, on `409fd51` and `0f2406f` (`refs/entire/checkpoints/*`, pushed). The remote ref SHAs differ from local, so re-push.
**Gaps:**
• Only **2 of 83 commits** are checkpointed (enabled on Oct 12), against the PRD's "CLI enabled for the whole build". The judge's effort-consistency and prompt-quality checks see only one session.
• The adversary-session checkpoint `01M4PYAG…` exists only in a scratch clone, not on main.
• `entire.json` lists 1 checkpoint (repoHead `409fd51`).
• The repo is private, so no checkpoint is visible. `git clone` does not fetch `refs/entire/*`. | | **cfo.ai (part of 25%)** | 2/10 | `docs/BUSINESS.md` plus `economics.json` hold real computed costs ($0.1263 model USD and 62 Crustdata credits over 4 live bundles). The plan is **not imported** (`plan` null; evidence status "pending"). The MCP work is in progress elsewhere. BUSINESS.md says "Cost per certificate not computable — report predates replays", which is a stale export. | | **Demo video (20%)** | 1/10 | Only `docs/media/notary-showreel.mp4`, a 15-second showreel of fixture numbers labelled "Measured on Notary's evaluation suite" with no "simulated" wording. The untracked `docs/video/SCRIPT.md` is 3:00 long, covers **none of the three mandatory sponsors**, and scene 5 says "This is a real run of the billing queue". **That is false**: q03 exists only as fixture data. | | **Building in public (15%)** | ?/10 | Nothing in the repo shows X posts. The user owns this. | | **Usefulness and originality (10%)** | 7/10 | Strong idea: live APIs, real per-call cost, commit-then-run, adversary, certificates and revocation. Transfer: `priors_applied` 15, `priors_informative` 3, but with-vs-without priors is not measured. Drift exists only on fixtures. | ### Submission checklist (BUILD_PLAN L299–310) - **Repo public:** MISSING. `gh` reports `"visibility":"PRIVATE"`, and GitHub returns 404 without auth. - **README links every number:** PARTIAL. The links exist, but the values are stale. - **Fresh-clone replay, no `.env`:** FAIL, exit 1 (section 3). - **Entire checkpoints pushed:** PARTIAL (2 refs). - **No secrets:** done (`check:secrets`; not re-run this pass). - **Seeded data and drift disclosed:** done for fixtures. The drift fixture is fixture-only. - **BUSINESS.md contains the cfo.ai plan:** PARTIAL. The file exists; the plan does not. - **Dashboard deployed on phone:** MISSING. `vercel.json` exists, nothing is deployed. - **~2.5-minute video covering all three sponsors:** MISSING. - **Quote-tweet, Discord post:** user, at 7:00 PM. ## 2. PRD headline metrics | Metric | Status | |---|---| | Unguarded call sites | **Real: 0.** Both the tsc and entire backends. | | Belief precision | **Real: 1, false beliefs 0.** Only n=1 on crustdata and n=4 on dodo, against the checker on the same recording (disclosed, A-14). | | Reproducibility | **Partial.** Exact match for 3 of 4 live bundles. The best is the crustdata notarize: 66 metrics plus all 5 record sections. EVALUATION picks the dodo 014032Z replay, which has 0 probes and is a weak example. `notarize-dodo-20261012T012315Z`, the only Dodo run with probes and the source of the Dodo certificates, **cannot replay** (CASSETTE MISS on the wallet ledger entry, DECISIONS #200). | | Cost | **Real per notarize run.** Cost per queue run (run 2 < run 1) is **not measured**. | | Unsafe actions, automation rate, noise floor | **Not measured.** They need the seed. | | Probes with vs without priors | **Not measured.** This is keyless now (`--compare-priors` replays `probes-dodo`). | | Drift un-learning | **Not measured on real data.** `make:drift` is keyless now that real cassettes exist. A-16 warns a fresh belief may not un-learn from 3 designs; report the outcome honestly either way. | **Strongest real result today:** on live Crustdata, the deterministic checker, with no model involved, found 3 places where the API contradicts its docs: - enrich no-match returns 400, not 200 empty; - identify no-match returns 400, not 200; - identify with invalid fields returns 403, not 400. Every probe committed its hashed prediction before the call and exported to neatlogs. The adversary narrowed every belief. The whole run replays offline exactly, for $0.039 and 62 credits. None of those 3 contradictions became a "contradicts docs" certificate: 2 anomalies were skipped and 1 was inconclusive. Probing them is cheap (400/403 responses likely cost no credits) and would give the first real contradicts-docs certificates. **What the core story still needs:** 1. The user runs `seed:dodo --wait-minutes 60` and completes the 12 hosted test-card checkouts. The README says 11 in L182 and 12 in L127. 2. `notarize --tool dodo --priors-from crustdata` again with the manifest, so the refund probes run. 3. `run --naive`, then `run` (guarded), then `export`, `export --certificates`, `economics`. **Warning:** real Dodo honored all 4 certified claims (units, idempotency, page clamp). The naive run may show **0 unsafe actions on real Dodo**; the "later page" case probably won't trip (DECISIONS #32). Prepare to tell it as "the guarded run holds refunds that lack certificates", with the 9→0 result shown only as the labelled evaluation suite with simulated APIs. The seeded world is single-use. ## 3. Fresh clone (`git clone` of the local repo, no `.env`, Windows, machine at about 93% CPU because another agent was running) | Step | Result | |---|---| | `pnpm install` | OK, 2m57s. Needs pnpm 11.7.0. | | `pnpm typecheck` | OK, 5m37s. | | `pnpm test` | **FAIL**, about 5m15s. Core: 981 passed, 4 failed, 5 skipped (6 failing files). Web: 2 failures, which pass when re-run alone, so they came from load. | | `pnpm notary replay` | **Exit 1** after 44s: `REPLAY FAILED: 1/4 bundle(s) did not reproduce, 7 verification failure(s)`. | | `pnpm notary demo --fixture` | OK, exit 0, 35s. | | `pnpm --filter @notary/web build` | OK, 2m23s. | **Deterministic test failures:** 2 in `test/publish.test.ts` (L221, L277). The committed `evidence.json` is built from state a clone does not have: gitignored `runs/*/spans.jsonl`, and `refs/entire/checkpoints`, which `git clone` does not fetch. So a clone regenerates "Entire pending" and fails. **Timeouts:** - `test/cli.test.ts` "export (no --sample)" hit its 5s timeout 3 times out of 3, even when run alone. - Hook timeouts in `incidents` and `ask-trace` (10s) and `coverage` (120s); `chat-safety` (5s). - These may pass on an idle machine, but they are borderline. **Replay problems:** - The 7 "TAMPERED OR INVALID BUNDLE" lines come from `discoverBundles` in `packages/core/src/replay/index.ts:291–296`. It parses `public/bundles/*.timeline.json` as bundles. To a judge, this reads as tampering. - Running replay a second time adds 3 "CONFLICT" errors (L302): the replay bundles written to `runs/` collide with the published `-replay` bundles. So replay is not idempotent. - The README's description of replay (L102: "finds the one bundle, the SAMPLE… exit 3") is wrong. ## 4. README and docs: stale statements, with exact lines **README.md** - Missing entirely: a dashboard link, a video link, screenshots and a real-results section. - L9: "No API keys were available… no live run has been recorded yet". - L67: "generated from 0 real bundles". - L73–81: every row "not measured yet". Belief precision, unguarded sites and reproducibility are measured now. - L89: "673 passed". - L102: replay description. - L149: neatlogs "No span has reached neatlogs". - L151: cfo.ai "Not started… Neither exists yet". - L152–153: Crustdata and Dodo "No live call yet". - L154: AWS Bedrock row. The models actually run through LiteLLM; there is no LiteLLM row; AWS is unused. - L181: "No API keys, so no results". - L182: "11 hosted test-card checkouts". - L187: "neatlogs is unverified. No span has been exported". - L189: "The dashboard isn't here yet… Codex… placeholder README". - L196: "Drift fixtures… None exist yet". - L210: "dashboard (Codex)". **hackathon.md** - L31: neatlogs "No notarize/run spans yet". - L32: Entire "pending, CLI not installed". - L33: cfo.ai "BUSINESS.md… not created yet". - L34–35: Crustdata and Dodo "blocked (no key)". - L37: LiteLLM "key pending". - L41: 673 tests. - L44–45: "0 real bundles". - L54. - L67: replay "BLOCKED, exit 3". It is now exit 1. - L68 and L71: checkbox states. **Other docs** - `docs/EVALUATION.md` L485: "`pnpm test` FAIL: 951 passed, 14 failed… (@notary/web has no tests yet)". This is a visible red flag. Regenerate it after fixing. - `docs/AUDIT.md` L5: "no real evidence…". L9–14: "0 cassettes". - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` L5: "no live run has been recorded". L36 and L191: Codex, placeholder. - `docs/PRD.md` L158 and L162: "build starts at 12:30 PM… nothing may predate". This conflicts with the hackathon.md resolution (see section 6). - `PLAN.md`: P10, U2 and U3 unchecked though the web work is done; the last Session 12 bullet (`export --entire`) is not reflected, because `entire.json` repoHead is still `409fd51` and lacks checkpoint `01M4Q2JS…`. - `packages/web/public/evidence/evidence.json`: the neatlogs purpose says "Bedrock calls… wrapBedrock" and the notes say "not been read back", which contradicts DECISIONS #204. - `docs/screenshots/`: 20 of 23 PNGs are from Oct 11 09:50, before the Session 12 redesign (#194). The 6 `*-dark.png` files show a dark theme that no longer exists. Only `incidents-*` are current. - `docs/ENTIRE.md`: the "GitHub repo is private" note, and "first checkpoints come from the first commit" (they exist now). - `docs/BUSINESS.md`: "Cost per certificate not computable". Re-run `export --certificates`, then `economics`. ## 5. Deployability and demo - **Vercel:** `packages/web/vercel.json` is valid and the build passes, but nothing is deployed (the user needs to log in). - Bug: the rewrites cover only `/app/*`, so a direct load or refresh of **`/docs` will 404**, and the README sends judges to `/docs`. - Minor: the no-cache headers leave out `/incidents` and `/economics.json`. - The hosted site is read-only by construction: static JSON, approvals read-only, the chat replay engine. - **AWS:** ECS Express scripts are ready but have never run (`docs/DEPLOY_AWS.md` says BLOCKED; no Docker image). It is optional; claim AWS modestly or not at all. **Proposed 2:30 demo script (real features only; fixture shots labelled on screen):** | Time | What to show | What to say | |---|---|---| | 0:00–0:12 | Hook: the fixture naive transcript with the banner "Fixture data — simulated APIs" on screen. | "Agents trust docs. When the tool moves money, that's the bug." | | 0:12–0:22 | Title card. | "Notary won't move money on anything it hasn't certified. Read, test, challenge, certify, enforce." | | 0:22–0:50 | Terminal replay of `notarize --tool crustdata` (keyless, exact). Then the `/app/run` transcript of the real bundle. | Show the 3 real contradictions: 400 vs 200, and 403 vs 400. "Found by code, not a model." | | 0:50–1:08 | neatlogs UI: a probe span with `notary.prediction` and its hash, then the agent-monitoring view (trace `b7944cd2…`) and `/app/incidents`. | "Every probe commits its prediction before the call. neatlogs holds the receipts." | | 1:08–1:25 | A certificate detail page (for example `dodo.wallet.idempotency-key-no-duplicate`): scope, probes, the Adversary (opus-4.6) narrowing it. | "A stronger model attacks every belief. All five were narrowed, not rubber-stamped." | | 1:25–1:45 | If the seed is done: the real guarded run with held refunds and evidence packs, plus the approval desk. If not: the fixture change-api revocation, with its banner. | "No certificate, no money moves." | | 1:45–2:00 | `entire status`, `git log` trailers, `entire checkpoint explain`, `guards coverage --backend entire` → 0 unguarded, and the Report page receipts. | Entire. | | 2:00–2:15 | `/app/business`: real cost per run ($0.0316 plus 15.5 credits) and the imported cfo.ai plan (tiers, runway). | cfo.ai. | | 2:15–2:30 | Chat agent answering with citations ("it can't move money"), then the repo plus `notary replay` showing OK. | Close with the public repo URL. | ## 6. Honesty and authenticity risks 1. **Start time.** 27 commits land before 12:30 PM IST Oct 10; the first is at 02:49. The repo's own PRD L158 says a 12:30 PM start and that "nothing may predate". The resolution against the Luma page and the email lives only in hackathon.md and AUDIT A-11. Disclose it in the README and get the organizers' confirmation in writing in Discord. 2. The draft video says "real run of the billing queue". That is false. 3. The showreel's "Measured on Notary's evaluation suite" doesn't say the APIs are simulated. 4. Replay prints "TAMPERED", and EVALUATION shows tests failing. Both look broken or faked. 5. Entire was enabled late, so the checkpoint history covers 2 of 83 commits. Say so plainly. 6. Fixture guarded decision accuracy is 0.4, against 0.75 naive, because holds count as wrong. Explain it before a judge spots it. 7. Unreplayable bundle `012315Z`. Disclose it, or re-record. 8. The README now *understates* the work, which is the reverse risk. ## Must-do before 7:00 PM IST (priority order) | # | Task | Owner | |---|---|---| | 1 | Make the repo public, re-push the Entire refs, and decide on the start-time disclosure. | user | | 2 | Dodo seed: 12 hosted checkouts. Then notarize dodo, run naive, run guarded, export (all of `export`, `--certificates`, `--evidence`, `--entire`, `economics`). | user plus code | | 3 | cfo.ai: import the plan (MCP or CSV) and re-run `economics`. | user plus the other agent | | 4 | Fix replay: skip `*.timeline.json` in `discoverBundles`; make replay idempotent (no CONFLICT); handle or disclose `012315Z` so a fresh-clone replay exits 0. | code | | 5 | Make `publish.test.ts` independent of local state (or commit the facts it needs), and raise the cli/export timeouts. Then a clean fresh-clone `pnpm test`. | code | | 6 | Rewrite the README top: real results, dashboard link, video, a fresh screenshot, sponsor table with neatlogs/Entire/cfo.ai/LiteLLM. Update hackathon.md, AUDIT bottom line, ARCHITECTURE, evidence.json; regenerate EVALUATION.md. | code | | 7 | Add the `/docs` rewrite to `vercel.json`; deploy on Vercel and add the URL to the README. | code, then user to deploy | | 8 | Record the 2:30 video from the script above. Fix SCRIPT.md scene 5. | user plus code | | 9 | Grab a neatlogs UI screenshot or URL (`notary trace-link`) and commit it. | user | | 10 | Keyless quick wins: `notarize --tool dodo --compare-priors --priors-from crustdata`; a real `make:drift` plus `replay --drift`; probe the 3 Crustdata contradictions. | code | | 11 | Regenerate the screenshots and delete the obsolete `*-dark.png` files. | code | | 12 | Building-in-public posts, the quote-tweet and the Discord post. | user | Scratch artifacts (logs) are in `C:\Users\PARTHC~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Parth-Chilwerwar-Desktop-notary\ff1243e8-a2bc-405f-820f-cf11571bb5d5\scratchpad\`: `test.clean.log`, `replay.log`, `demo.log` and the `fresh\` clone. No repo files were edited.
